# Dependency upgrade review — 2026-09-27

Research snapshot: branch `codex/deps`, source revision `3c0ea1fcb6b352ef14e2b2a107e84328c666778d`. Finish line: a cited upgrade decision for every requested runtime and every direct root pub dependency, tied to this app's actual call sites. Non-goal: dependency edits, installation, deployment or release. Only this report and `COMMIT_MSG.txt` are produced.

“Latest” means the observed stable upstream publication on **2026-09-27**, excluding drafts/RCs/edge builds. For caret constraints, the installed baseline is `pubspec.lock`, not the lower bound. Pub “behind” counts stable semantic versions between resolved and latest; GitHub commit counts are full comparisons and include unrelated monorepo work. Cross-major Node and OS comparisons are explicitly not linear patch backlogs. **UPGRADE NOW** means prioritize a bounded implementation and its listed verification; no upgrade or phone validation was performed here.

The [full change inventory](#full-change-inventory) preserves upstream changes without filtering for app relevance; the recommendation and impact analysis remain separate.

The central AI Team finding: stable Gas City is only five commits ahead; most requested improvements remain on unreleased `main`. The pinned Gastown SHA is still the latest published pack. Per-session cost already exists in the pinned runtime and needs app integration, while undo-approval is not supplied by a new core REST endpoint.

## Upgrade now — ordered by app value and risk

These are separate candidate changes; keep diagnosis and rollback attributable. Exact source/version evidence and compatibility details follow in the component notes.

1. **mobile_scanner 7.4.0 → 7.4.2.** Change the exact root pubspec pin and resolve the lockfile with the pinned Flutter. This fixes a decoder stall, camera initialization crashes, orientation handling and the AGP 9 KGP warning without an identified Dart API rewrite. Re-run `test/kit/kit_scanner_test.dart` and `test/pairing_scanner_test.dart`; on physical arm64 test offline/no-Play-Services QR scanning, camera denial/in-use, 180-degree rotation, background/resume, exit/re-entry and release shrinking. Confirm camera/sensor resources stop. [Release changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/mobile_scanner/versions/7.4.2/changelog).
2. **Paseo 0.9.1 → 0.9.2.** Change `lib/termux/bridge.dart:3190` (`localAgentsPins['paseo_version']`), retain the independently justified `clientAppVersion=0.8.0`. Re-run `test/local_agent_runtime_test.dart`, `test/paseo_gateway_test.dart`, `test/local_agent_onboarding_test.dart`; validate the actual install/repair path, native node-pty, Claude create/send/stream/approve/cancel, repeated disconnect/reconnect, restart and stale-PID recovery on arm64/proot. Measure idle CPU and RSS over connection churn. Repair also updates unpinned Claude Code, so record that version rather than attributing every change to Paseo. [Release](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/releases/tag/v0.9.2).
3. **Dio 5.11.0 → 5.11.1 through its generator pin.** The app caret already allows it; `packages/opencode_sdk/pubspec.yaml:12` fixes the effective version. Change `tool/sdk/templates/pubspec.mustache:16` and `tool/sdk/templates/README.mustache:30`, regenerate with `tool/sdk/generate.sh`, then update root/package resolutions. Never hand-edit generated SDK output. Verify deterministic regeneration, SDK `dart analyze` / `dart test`, `test/api2_transport_test.dart`, `test/api2_sse_test.dart`, `test/connection_sse_*_test.dart`, `test/server_probe_test.dart`, and Gas City/quota streams. Exercise a paused large response and cancellation against a local server to establish bounded buffering; small mocks alone cannot prove backpressure. [Changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/dio/versions/5.11.1/changelog).
4. **flutter_secure_storage 11.0.0 → 11.2.0.** Change the exact root pin and resolve its platform interface >=2.1.0 together. Multi-instance key handling matters to profile, orchestration and external-agent stores. Re-run `test/profile_secure_storage_test.dart`, `test/profile_store_test.dart` and related external-agent/team-store tests using the required secure-storage method-channel mock. Device validation must preserve real existing credentials across restart, concurrent stores and deletion of one profile. Keep namespaces/options unchanged. `checkUpgradeStatus()` is optional future re-pairing UX; the bump cannot restore credentials previously lost by skipping v10. [Changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_secure_storage/versions/11.2.0/changelog).
5. **OpenCode 1 1.18.29 → 1.18.32.** Update `TermuxRuntime`, `defaultOpenCodeVersion` and shell fallback pins together (`lib/termux/bridge.dart:13,69,1637,1904`). Re-run `test/termux_scripts_test.dart`, `test/termux_runtime_switch_test.dart`, `test/managed_runtime_switch_preflight_test.dart`, generated SDK checks, and an authenticated chat/SSE/provider-image smoke. Gas City ACP load/resume/fork is the key additional regression surface. Test existing-install explicit setup/update as well as fresh install; switching to an already-installed runtime does not update it. [Compare](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/compare/v1.18.29...v1.18.32).
6. **Dolt 2.3.3 → 2.3.5.** Change `AiTeamPins.dolt` and both Linux asset hashes/byte counts (`lib/builtin/setup/aiteam_scripts.dart:44,80,107`); archive layout is unchanged. Release asset metadata: arm64 SHA256 `9ce70fc81e50139e97758ef7f4dc57e9583e4e5ef05ad75d7535c30caa161387`, 40,789,338 bytes; amd64 `c49d4c3e004cf1581ba0d4a00c5023a26f84eb2ec15d5fe876eed36d5343f463`, 44,023,897 bytes. Re-verify downloaded bytes before implementing. Run `test/aiteam_component_test.dart`, `test/builtin_team_test.dart`, `test/builtin_team_hot_test.dart`, then copied existing-store reopen, fresh city, interrupted startup/restart, claim→close→merge and integrity checks on arm64. Keep this patch separate from the Beads schema migration. Legacy Android-native manifests need their own artifact provenance; Linux digests cannot replace native-build digests. [Release](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/tag/v2.3.5).
7. **Termux Ubuntu Base 24.04.4 → 24.04.5; retain Noble.** Update filenames/checksums and marker at `lib/termux/bridge.dart:1578–1611`, preserving the 24.04 URL. Canonical SHA256: arm64 `a91d5a93010193712d346d761372b7c9db6dfcf093893161c64ca107f05914f2`; armhf `4fcee4d278f1c5232e085a021a85e4c6cef3853557a88d98ff380b5e5d5841bb`; amd64 `e77b6f10c2590cef872b33ee9f635a0e3fd1f57fb074c0e52b5c7f56147a0c86`. Future implementation gates: follow the focused checks above first; at a stable candidate, pinned Flutter `pub get`, clean analyzer, complete serial test manifest, and generated-SDK checks when affected. Native dependency changes need Android release-mode compilation and device validation; signing/delivery remain outside this research. No Flutter or native test process was launched for this documentation-only work.

## Per-component notes — Priority 1: AI Team

### Gas City 1.4.1 → 1.4.2 and Gastown pack

Evidence: `gh release list/view` and `gh api .../compare` plus complete upstream git history. Gas City main was frozen at `93a24f0354333480d81372ea0076b277a4a3b3f7`; packs main at `556effb4b2c5275063d145b783271f6608d09e42`. The Gas City `edge` prerelease is not stable. Packs has no GitHub Release objects: **do not confuse the repository-wide `v0.4.0` tag with the Gastown package version**. That tag is 96 repository commits / 5 Gastown commits after the pin, but the authoritative registry still publishes Gastown 0.1.10 at the app's SHA. [Gas City stable release](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/releases/tag/v1.4.2), [stable compare](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/compare/v1.4.1...v1.4.2), [main compare](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/compare/v1.4.1...93a24f0354333480d81372ea0076b277a4a3b3f7), [frozen pack registry](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/blob/556effb4b2c5275063d145b783271f6608d09e42/registry.toml#L44-L118), [pack compare](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/compare/33d3a430a67d1782ad364556cb566bdb01d0afe3...556effb4b2c5275063d145b783271f6608d09e42).

#### What 1.4.2 actually changes

The five commits update native/CLI Beads integration to 1.3.0, accept its decimal-string revision format, document/test schema migration, renew runtime security waivers, and fix graph self-close/failure cleanup. Fresh managed workspaces initialize against Beads 1.3.0; failed workflow scopes close skipped work and execute cleanup. The compiler correction only affects **newly instantiated graphs**, not persisted graph dependencies. This can fix run completion, but is not an agent-start performance release. No `internal/api/` or generated OpenAPI file changes exist in the stable diff; the app's HTTP endpoints and DTO fields have no identified stable breaking delta. [Compatibility change](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/dea5e5867), [graph completion change](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/d45821663).

The release directs shared database upgrades to stop/co-ordinate all clients and run `bd migrate schema` (schema **53 → 66**); old clients cannot read the migrated database. Thus a version/checksum replacement alone is insufficient. Review together with the Beads section's known 1.3.0 migration defect; do not let different app/host installations open a newly migrated city with 1.2.2. The affected setup entry points are `lib/builtin/setup/aiteam_scripts.dart:41` (versions/downloads/checks), `lib/builtin/team/builtin_team.dart:319` (existing-city/create path), `:413` (rig initialization), and `lib/termux/team_scripts.dart:135` (shared downloaded pins). Existing databases are outside the Dart type system: passing DTO tests cannot prove migration safe. [Migration notes](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/releases/tag/v1.4.2).

**Security caveat, not a clean-security upgrade:** v1.4.1 `go.mod` carries gRPC 1.82.1; v1.4.2 carries 1.83.0. Main explicitly fixes **GO-2026-6348** (reachable HTTP/2 fragmentation OOM) and **CVE-2026-84445 / GO-2026-6443** by moving 1.83.0 → 1.83.2. That security fix is absent from 1.4.2. Do not claim a newer stable tarball automatically fixes its Go dependencies, or claim internet exploitability of the phone's loopback topology without checking reachable paths. Upstream release waiver renewal is not a vulnerability fix. [Upstream security fix and validation](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/550240d32), [v1.4.2 module](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/v1.4.2/go.mod), [waiver renewal](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/62e5f65da).

#### Exact app contract and unreleased impact

The main OpenAPI comparison preserves all route paths from 1.4.1. Changes relevant here are additive fields/headers and runtime semantics rather than a wholesale REST version change. Nevertheless, a main build is **not** a supported substitute for 1.4.2: storage, lifecycle and dispatch implementations changed substantially.

| `/runs`, `/convoys`, `/bead/{id}`, `/beads?ready=true&rig=...`, `/waits`, `/pending`: `gascity_gateway.dart:247,288,410,445` | Stable graph completion changes may make new runs terminate correctly. #### Known traps: fixed where, still not proven on this phone

- **File store:** `docs/qa/ai-team/spike-pc-2026-09.md:99` reports file-store CLI/claim failure and cross-rig duplicate IDs. Main's [rig-scoped file prefixes](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/c6c29004d) specifically fixes duplicate IDs, **not evidence that the full pinned Gastown/Dolt workflow now runs file-only**. Main separately adds a [pure-Go SQLite store](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/f23b9e8f0) and [per-class storage bindings](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/7cf3bfcb3). This is a possible future phone experiment to reduce coordination overhead, not authorization to remove Dolt or migrate existing work silently. None is in 1.4.2.
- **Rig add:** stable CLI remains path-first `gc rig add "$project" --name "$rig"`; our `builtin_team.dart:413` already uses the correct form and does bounded retries. Main [fixes managed-Dolt dirty-table initialization deadlock](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/9fb7af13b), a different trap from the spike's wrong positional invocation. Do not remove retry/recovery based only on stable 1.4.2. `gc init --file ./city.toml --name ... --no-start city` (`builtin_team.dart:358`), `gc import install` (`:440`), `gc supervisor run` (`:601`) and `gc order run` upkeep calls (`:269`) retain their verbs/flags.
- **Orphan MCP and false lifecycle kills:** spike §4.6 measured two orphan MCP processes burning CPU after agents died. Main [fences destructive actions on unknown liveness](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/3f924d2a7), [refuses uncorroborated orphan kills](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/da84dbfed), [protects city Dolt/watchdog/proxy infrastructure during orphan kills](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/2332772d2), and [adds bounded, identity-fenced, subreaper-aware termination of wedged drained seats](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/6becabe41). These address process-tree safety and eventual cleanup but do not constitute a verified fix of this app's specific OpenCode/MCP orphan scenario under proot. The app's process grouping remains at `lib/termux/bridge.dart:2837` and supervisor lifecycle in `lib/termux/team_scripts.dart:938`.
- **Phantom sessions versus Android phantom-process killer are different:** main [recycles dead named sessions holding work](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/fa8c704fb) and [wedged claim holders without progress](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/bccc52f61). Neither exempts Android background/phantom-process limits or proves Android will preserve a high-process-count team. The current phone tuning disables extra agents/orders and runs bounded upkeep (`builtin_team.dart:206,217,236`); keep it pending measurements.
- **Cold ACP starts:** main [skips irrelevant startup-dialog polling for OpenCode](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/fe461a2c0) and [fences ACP startup ownership/rollback](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/81363b907). It does not remove OpenCode's per-agent process, establish ACP attach support, or justify deleting our worktree/plugin cache wrapper (`aiteam_scripts.dart:146-197`) and longer phone handshake/startup timeouts.

#### Performance and Android/arm64/proot compatibility

1.4.2 ships `gascity_1.4.2_linux_arm64.tar.gz` (40,837,782 bytes) and linux_amd64 (43,977,000 bytes), with upstream SHA256 list. The pinned arm64 archive is 26,032,922 bytes (`aiteam_scripts.dart:68`): **+14,804,860 bytes / +56.9% download**, not evidence of improved memory. Go binaries are built `CGO_ENABLED=0`; Linux arm64 exists but is not Android-native support. App comments `aiteam_scripts.dart:9-13` record SIGSYS/faccessat2 for direct Android execution; run the Linux build inside the existing proot Ubuntu and retain the execute-once install guard. This review downloaded/read source and metadata only; it did not run a new binary on arm64 or a phone. [Release assets](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/releases/tag/v1.4.2), [build configuration](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/v1.4.2/.goreleaser.yml).

Main's credible phone-relevant candidates are [store-free SSE send loop](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/631929f41) (avoids serial `bd show` process creation for unrelated stores), [bounded archive filtering](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/0e6462a36) (upstream 176s→1s workload; directly hits our `/events?type=convoy.closed&since=...` at `gascity_gateway.dart:296`), [single config load per store open](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/3d482b33b), [avoid reparsing pack TOML each tick](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/13886fbee), [memoize pack validation](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/036f05ae0), [back off process snapshots](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/d6e867a6f), [bound idle Dolt connections](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/8304178b7) and [close dispatch stores to prevent unbounded WAL](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/ac8f6c6cd). They reduce work in mechanisms especially expensive under proot; there is **no measured phone RSS/latency improvement** from them yet. The historical local phone evidence remains ~79 MB supervisor, 96 MB Dolt, 28 MB watchdog, 563 MB ACP worker (`docs/qa/team-hot-2026-09-26/README.md:36`); new-runtime benchmarks must use the same workload.

#### Gastown pack: what an eventual new published pin should include

Already on published 0.1.10; do not change to the moving `main` branch or repo-wide `v0.4.0` and describe that as a new supported Gastown release. The 28 unpublished directory commits contain substantial useful fixes:

- [Claim/ownership/restart verification and duplicate-work prevention](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/44b2eef), [route shipped `bd` commands through `gc`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/9b4df3e), [molecule instead of invalid wisp type](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/1407301).
- [Witness rechecks live status before deletion; verifies rebased/squashed merges by content](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/05031f2), [crashed submit-and-exit handoff recovery](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/b43abe6), [refinery survives its own claim](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/cd0078f).
- [Local-only base branch support](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/e72252e), [require actual branch commits before handoff](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/3c15b64), [fail closed when no-push configuration lacks auto_push](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/ef28498): directly relevant to our local-origin setup (`builtin_team.dart:424`) and merge/branch truth.
- [Boot patrol loop avoids hot respawning](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/0f35a61), [bounded single-flight status queries](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/a21effc), [remove ineffective refinery sleep_after_idle](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/ef66088), [default polecat workflow](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity-packs/commit/3d7d6d5). These may change phone agent activity/power use, not just text.

Pack content is shell/TOML/prompts and has no architecture-specific binary. Its exact CLI/formula compatibility and actual process count need a matched `gc`/`bd` evaluation; the current registry does not publish a newer Gastown release or prove its main snapshot works with our old runtime. Existing hooks `worktree-setup.sh ... --sync` (`aiteam_scripts.dart:173-175`), `gastown.polecat` routing and disabled patrol overrides are the concrete integration points.

#### Recommended future candidate and checks

Keep **gc 1.4.1 + registered Gastown 0.1.10 SHA** for this research-only change. Queue a **coordinated, backed-up migration candidate** around a stable Gas City release containing Beads schema fixes and patched gRPC, then the new published Gastown version when available. If evaluating today's 1.4.2, use exact linux_arm64/amd64 assets + updated hashes/size/member values in `AiTeamPins`, compatible Beads and copied/restorable city data; do not call the 1,145-commit main delta a patch update. Preserve/archive or deliberately regenerate legacy `assets/aiteam/manifest*.json` and `tool/host/aiteam-manifest*.json` records rather than leaving apparently-current contradictory pins.

Focused future checks: `test/aiteam_component_test.dart`, `test/builtin_team_test.dart`, `test/builtin_team_hot_test.dart`, `test/builtin_team_bring_in_test.dart`, `test/termux_aiteam_script_test.dart`, `test/termux_aiteam_upstream_test.dart`, `test/team_gascity_gateway_test.dart`, `test/team_gascity_mappers_test.dart`, `test/team_control_test.dart`, `test/team_controls_*test.dart`, team board/work-edit tests and fixture/host-front tests. Live copied-city proof: fresh initialization + migrated city reopen; two rigs with distinct prefixes; create/claim/output/restart/pending response/cancel/reopen/merge; SSE resume with a busy event backlog; abrupt worker/supervisor exit preserves Dolt and reaps only attributed MCP children; measure task-to-first-output, full team RSS, process count and idle CPU on arm64/proot. No tests were run for this research fragment.

### Beads 1.2.2 → 1.3.0 — UPGRADE LATER, as a coordinated AI Team store migration

**Evidence and counting.** Pin: `lib/builtin/setup/aiteam_scripts.dart:43`; Linux arm64/amd64 artifacts at lines 73/100; version check at 218. `gh release list` reports 1.3.0 (2026-09-15) as the newest non-prerelease; 1.3.1-rc.1 is deliberately excluded. GitHub [compare v1.2.2…v1.3.0](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/compare/v1.2.2...v1.3.0) reports **1,350 commits**. The [1.3.0 release](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0) explicitly says 1.2.2 is essentially the 1.1.2-era tree: it withheld the 1.2.1 changes. Read both `[1.2.1]` and `[1.3.0]` in the [tagged changelog](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.3.0/CHANGELOG.md); release-number distance badly understates this upgrade.

**Useful app improvements.** Work leases (`heartbeat`, `reclaim`, `unclaim`) give recovery for an agent dying mid-task; conditional `update --if-assignee/--if-status` avoids reassignment races. The release fixes claim-family server writes by verifying them, expired deferred tasks not waking, ready-queue filters being silently ignored, and dependency/wisp migration corruption. Those matter to task state shown by `lib/orchestration/adapters/gascity/dto/bead.dart` and board actions in `lib/orchestration/adapters/gascity/gascity_work_edits.dart:50,60,73,81,92`; the app reaches them through Gas City, so the Beads binary alone does not add a board “lease” UI. A new `bd serve` API (41 operations /35 paths), optional bearer-token file, structured errors, version guards, opt-in durable journal, and batched operations offer future integration possibilities. They are not the existing Gas City `/v0` adapter and must not be substituted without a new gateway contract.

**Concrete break surface.** Existing local stores go main schema **53→66** plus clone-local **0011→0026**, about 28 migration steps. Shared SQL-server stores refuse implicit migration; updated clients read, but writes require explicit `bd migrate schema` (or deliberately scoped consent). All clients sharing the store must move together; older binaries then fail forward-schema checks. Back up with the **old** binary before installing, including Dolt history/config if required, and rehearse rollback on a copy. App installer `AiTeamScripts.install` (`aiteam_scripts.dart:230`) currently installs programs; `BuiltinTeam.cityScript` (`lib/builtin/team/builtin_team.dart:320`) skips an already-ready city at 327 and has no upgrade-migration journey. Its destructive fresh-city retries at 353–358 are **not** an acceptable migration recovery path. A pin-only upgrade can therefore leave an apparently installed AI Team unable to write.

Other upstream CLI breaks: `bd update --status <done>` now checks close policy; `search` includes closed issues; scripted empty-ID `update/close` fails; silent git-origin Dolt-remote adoption now requires consent; `dep cycles --json` changes its shape; `--profile` becomes `--cpu-profile`; `delete --force` on a team server orphans dependents rather than deleting their subtree; explicit server port overrides `BEADS_DOLT_PORT`. Our Dart tree does **not** call these CLI flags/parsers directly (it invokes `bd --version`, `bd metrics off`, and delegates actual task operations to Gas City). However, `cancelWork` first writes `close_reason=cancelled` at `gascity_work_edits.dart:73` then invokes `/close` at 81; validate blocked/open-child cancellation and refusal behavior after the underlying close-policy change. Gas Town formulas also invoke Beads: current evidence at `docs/qa/ai-team/spike-pc-2026-09.md:96` lists `bd ready --assignee`, `gc bd update --claim`, `bd close`, so pack/GC compatibility is a real dependency even when Dart has no direct flag use.

**Phone performance.** The changelog removes unconditional telemetry work on every CLI invocation (lazy/cached machine ID and no detached metrics child unless queued, throttled to five minutes). Our scripts already set `BD_DISABLE_METRICS=1` (`lib/builtin/team/builtin_team.dart:314`, `aiteam_scripts.dart:361`), so avoiding work despite opt-out is relevant. Server auto-backup now defaults off, and batched/off auto-commit finally works in direct SQL-server mode; these reduce repeated work only when that topology/configuration applies. The new proxied-server mode can reap an idle backend after 30 seconds: upstream's one-host measurements were 130 MB→0 idle for one workspace and 2,456 MB→0 for 20, but active proxied mode consumed **more** RAM (3,445 vs 2,483 MB at 20) and added 0.30–0.63 s cold starts. These are upstream desktop measurements and require an explicit topology migration; do not claim automatic phone RAM savings from a pin bump.

**Security.** [PR #6047](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/6047) says Go 1.26.7 release binaries close seven reachable stdlib advisories relative to the prior build toolchain: GO-2026-6218 / CVE-2026-56860 (`net/url` quadratic resolution), GO-2026-6091 / CVE-2026-56858 (template regexp context), GO-2026-6090 / CVE-2026-56862 (TLS post-handshake resource use), GO-2026-6089 / CVE-2026-56853 (HTTP/2 header timeout), GO-2026-6088 / CVE-2026-56859 (XML recursion), GO-2026-5972 / CVE-2026-33818 (ASN.1 recursion), and GO-2026-5026 / CVE-2026-39821 (IDNA). Aliases verified in the [Go vulnerability database](https://vuln.go.dev/ID/GO-2026-6218.json) and corresponding ID records. Exploitability varies: this app does not launch the new `bd serve`, disables metrics, and uses local managed stores. The release also stops silent Dolt-remote adoption and config reads leaking memory keys. The other dependency-advisory fixes are largely tooling/test-only per upstream; do not present all 25 as exposed phone vulnerabilities.

**Compatibility / blocker.** 1.3.0 publishes both Linux arm64 and Android arm64, but the current app expects the **Linux/glibc build inside proot**. Keep that artifact; the Android artifact is not a drop-in reason to redesign lifecycle. Release Linux-arm64 size grows from pinned 45,556,402 to 49,272,237 bytes (~3.7 MB compressed). Current [phone spike](../qa/ai-team/spike-phone-2026-09.md) records Android `faccessat2`/SIGSYS and phantom-process issues outside proot; no Beads note removes Android's process killer. Latest stable also has a [known missing-events-table bug #6142](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6142): reads work but mutations fail, with the sentinel-floor fix [#6547](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/6547) held for 1.3.1. Proxied mode lacks its own backup path and `bd dolt start` is not proxy-aware. Qualify Gas City+pack+Beads together, or wait for stable 1.3.1; do not ship the RC as “latest stable.” Verify fresh/existing stores, every board mutation, restart after killed worker, concurrent claim/reclaim, migration refusal/backup/restore, and real arm64 process/RSS/thermal behavior.

**Approval reversal cross-check.** Beads 1.3.0 also has no dedicated `unapprove`/undo-approval verb: its [registered gate commands](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.3.0/cmd/bd/gate.go#L1275-L1282) are list/create/show/resolve/check/add-waiter. Current main at `4213c229a4ec72aed8b1875be14a428fa8e150a3` is the same. Generic [`bd reopen`](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/4213c229a4ec72aed8b1875be14a428fa8e150a3/cmd/bd/reopen.go#L16-L20) can reopen a closed gate, potentially through `gc bd`, but does not establish reversal of a Gas City approval, dispatch or execution. Historical references to gate approval commands are not evidence of a current semantic undo API.

### Dolt 2.3.3 → 2.3.5 — UPGRADE NOW

`AiTeamPins.dolt` is at `aiteam_scripts.dart:44`. [Compare](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/compare/v2.3.3...v2.3.5) contains **105 commits**, and the [2.3.4](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/tag/v2.3.4) and [2.3.5](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/tag/v2.3.5) notes are the two intervening releases. Most changes are SQL correctness, not new mobile UX.

The strongest direct benefit is [journal-writer bootstrap cancellation race #11796](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/pull/11796): the current app repeatedly starts/stops managed Dolt, and city initialization explicitly handles partial starts (`lib/builtin/team/builtin_team.dart:347–358`). Other relevant maintenance includes persisted `sql_mode` surviving restart, cached branch/tag name indexes, and fixes for foreign-key column drops, legacy table-name unmarshalling and query evaluation. LOAD_FILE directory-handle leaks are fixed, but our tree has no LOAD_FILE call, so this is not evidence of our observed phone RAM issue. New replication wildcard filtering and PostgreSQL adaptive-JSON behavior are not used by this app. Release benchmark tables compare against MySQL, **not 2.3.3**, and establish no phone speedup.

There is no announced `dolt version`, `dolt config --global --add`, or managed SQL-server CLI break in this patch range. Those are the direct integration points (`aiteam_scripts.dart:219,357–360`; managed process matching in `lib/builtin/team/builtin_team.dart:353` and `lib/termux/bridge.dart:2559,2771`). Beads/Gas City own SQL/schema interaction. The gRPC security item in the 2.3.4 notes changes `integration-tests/go-sql-server-driver`, so do not claim a production Dolt CVE remediation from it. No runtime CVE is asserted for this two-patch range.

Linux arm64/amd64 release assets retain the expected `dolt-linux-<arch>/bin/dolt` members. No Android/proot support promise is added; run the existing startup smoke on actual arm64. Current `docs/qa/ai-team/spike-pc-2026-09.md:96–102` shows why Dolt remains required: Gas Town shell formulas need a real Beads store and the file store reused IDs across scopes. Dolt 2.3.5 does not remove that architectural trap.


## Per-component notes — Priority 2: other runtimes

### OpenCode 1: 1.18.29 → 1.18.32

**Evidence.** `npm view opencode-ai version` returned 1.18.32; GitHub stable releases are 1.18.30, .31 and .32, with 104 commits in the [exact tag comparison](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/compare/v1.18.29...v1.18.32). The count is the entire monorepo, including hosted Console/docs, not 104 mobile-runtime changes. [1.18.30 notes](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.18.30), [1.18.31 notes](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.18.31), [1.18.32 notes](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases/tag/v1.18.32).

**App value.** .30 adds the GPT-6 Astra system prompt and GitLab effort variants, preserves Bedrock DeepSeek/ARN model IDs, updates OpenAI/Azure SDK compatibility and preserves explicit OpenAI service tiers. .31 restores model/effort/mode and reasoning boundaries across ACP load/resume/fork. That matters when Gas City drives OpenCode through ACP, while this app's own model catalog/variants use `lib/api/product_repository.dart:1420,1443` and attachment capabilities `:1462`. .32 fixes Together streaming usage and Bedrock tool-image handling. The release prose and underlying Bedrock commit are not worded identically; the commit is the source of truth for the conditional image transformation ([c101347](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c10134729dd2ce00beb18604ec91f10319f59a78)). These are provider/agent correctness improvements, not a demonstrated mobile frame-rate or RSS improvement.

**Breaking/security impact.** No removed HTTP endpoint/DTO field or `serve --hostname --port` flag was identified in the tag diff. The managed invocation remains `lib/termux/bridge.dart:1068-1071`; setup selects the Linux binary package at `lib/termux/opencode_ubuntu_setup.dart:49-64`. ACP is the most important behavioral regression area. A hosted Console inference-proxy authentication fix exists in the monorepo diff, but must not be represented as a security fix to the installed mobile server. No CVE was named in these release notes.

**Android/proot.** npm publishes `opencode-linux-arm64@1.18.32` and x64 plus musl variants. Our installer selects Linux/glibc inside Ubuntu, not a native Android/Bionic executable. No published evidence here promises proot support or changed phone memory use; smoke the exact arm64 binary before adoption. **Verdict: UPGRADE NOW**, with the focused integration checks above.

### OpenCode 2: 2.0.10 → 2.0.18

**Evidence and release ambiguity.** `npm view @opencode/cli version` returned 2.0.18; `v2.0.11` through `v2.0.18` tags exist and [the tag comparison](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/compare/v2.0.10...v2.0.18) reports 284 commits. `gh release view v2.0.18` returned “release not found”; do not confuse the repository's 1.18.32 GitHub release list with the independently published 2.x npm line. The exact tag trees and protocol/server/CLI diffs were read from a temporary upstream checkout because GitHub's compare file list is capped and omitted relevant late-alphabet packages.

**Concrete blocker — pairing.** [One-time server pairing](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/eccf0b3b7b70) replaces `opencode2 pair`'s `{urls, username, password}` JSON QR with `http(s)://host/auth/connect/:code` links. Upstream [CLI implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.18/packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/pair.ts) issues `POST /api/pair`; redeeming `GET /auth/connect/:code` with `Accept: application/json` returns `{token}`. That token is usable as the Basic-auth password, expires after 30 days, and is revoked by server password rotation ([auth implementation](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.0.18/packages/server/src/auth.ts)). Our `lib/state/pairing.dart:126,142,224` sniffs and requires the old JSON/password shape; `lib/ui/screens/pairing_scanner_screen.dart:132` calls the same parser. New upstream QR codes therefore cannot complete our current scan/paste journey. A runtime-only bump leaves an advertised user path broken even though old saved Basic-password connections continue working (`lib/api2/transport.dart:37,54,76`). Future work must safely parse/redeem the one-time link, store/consume the returned credential, handle expiry/reuse and re-pairing without leaking codes, preserve old payload compatibility, and test `pairing_payload`, `pairing_scanner`, `server_pairing_paste` and existing saved-server auth/reconnect. The initial redemption is outside the normal `/api` transport prefix; do not accidentally request `/api/auth/connect/...`.

**Other concrete protocol changes.** The tag diff adds optional session update `metadata` and durable `session.metadata.updated`; our `lib/api2/events.dart:414` safely represents unknown events but does not project that metadata. Credential DTOs add required server-produced `method: key|oauth`; projects add `time.active`; shell info adds optional `signal`. These are additive outputs, not evidence that our permissive decoders fail. Extend consumers only when product behavior needs them. Prompt/inbox endpoints used at `lib/api2/client.dart:260,285,291,295,299` remain present. “Undo queued prompts back into input” ([beeb14e](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/beeb14e91077)) is an upstream UI feature built around existing inbox operations; it does not automatically add our own restore-to-composer UI.

**Runtime value.** Relevant commits fix batched delta ordering before a new content block ([32d3535](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/32d3535f6684)), relax model WebSocket idle timeout/honor chunk timeout ([affa57e](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/affa57e40f44)), normalize AI SDK fragment boundaries, preserve child prompt-cache affinity, keep GPT-6 Sol/Luna cache across effort switches, repair legacy-media compaction checkpoints, surface signaled shell exits and improve several provider schemas/reasoning budgets. These affect our streamed chat/SSE and long-running sessions (`lib/api2/events.dart:236-279`, `lib/api2/gateway.dart:429`). New provider-account switching, Console device-flow/OAuth and Console-managed policies warrant provider/MCP permission verification; new image/video/speech/transcription routes are future optional capabilities, not features this app obtains from a pin change. TUI transcript virtualization/fs.watch fixes benefit terminals running that TUI, not Flutter rendering.

**Security/compatibility.** Debug-config credential redaction ([c98d9c6](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/c98d9c65dc47)) and patched OpenTelemetry core ([dddb5eb](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/dddb5eb96f80)) are security-relevant; no CVE identifier was established from those commit titles alone. New pairing avoids handing the long-lived password to each pairing client, but adoption requires correct token lifecycle. npm publishes `@opencode/cli-linux-arm64@2.0.18`; Ubuntu/glibc/proot remains necessary in this app, with no verified new phone performance guarantee. Keep `serve` flags, loopback binding and existing auth unchanged during any future upgrade. **Verdict: UPGRADE LATER**, paired with the pairing journey and serial `api2_*`, auth/provider/MCP, runtime-switch and phone smoke validation, then update `bridge.dart:14,1638,1905` together.

### Paseo daemon and client advertisement

**Evidence.** [0.9.2 release](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/releases/tag/v0.9.2) is non-prerelease; npm `latest` and `beta` both point to 0.9.2, so the presence of a beta dist-tag does not make this a prerelease. [0.9.1…0.9.2 comparison](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/compare/v0.9.1...v0.9.2) contains 55 commits. Pin provenance and previous actual Claude verification are documented locally at `lib/termux/bridge.dart:3178-3182`.

**Phone value.** [9978988](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/commit/9978988e35409a018a52d0d7646f18b51e562346) fixes daemon memory growth when client connections close, directly relevant to Android foreground/background and network churn. [c3e1e08](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/commit/c3e1e084a068e5895710c43b034ced8ebef256e8) fixes a Linux observation reconciliation hang after ignored directories appear; [#5170](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/pull/5170) cuts polling when filesystem observation is unavailable. Fewer retained sessions and less background polling are plausible phone RSS/battery wins, not measured results. Other server fixes preserve workspace records when disks/network shares disappear, prevent duplicate durable history after refresh, settle Pi/OMP cancellation when runtime already exited, fix archived logs and stale/recycled PID startup, and avoid plugin errors crashing the daemon.

**Our calls and breakage assessment.** The compare shows no protocol source removal/change (protocol package version only). Existing `fetch_agents_request` (`lib/paseo/gateway.dart:306`), `fetch_agent_timeline_request` (`:440`), `send_agent_message_request` (`:519`), `create_agent_request` (`:554`), mode/model setters (`:609,:620`), cancel (`:631`), permission response (`:675`) and live event switch (`:966-991`) therefore have no identified shape break in this patch. Structured Claude launch `providerOptions.extraArgs` is newly supported as string-or-null map, not raw argv; our creation payload at `:556-570` sends no such option, so this is optional future capability. Multi-select question and Android Back fixes in upstream's own React Native app are **not** fixes to our Flutter UI. Permission-rule handling for OpenCode agents and Codex Default/Read-only mode routing were fixed in daemon providers; recheck approvals if those providers are used through Paseo. No release-note CVE was identified.

**Compatibility.** The same Claude SDK version (0.3.246) remains in the server manifest, reducing one source of provider churn. Our command remains `paseo start --foreground --home … --listen … --no-relay --no-web-ui --no-inject-mcp` at `lib/termux/bridge.dart:3861`; no removal was identified. Native `node-pty` still needs the Ubuntu/glibc arm64 prebuild or local compiler fallback (`:3732,:3790-3797`). Linux support is not a promise of native Android support; rerun the on-phone checks. **Daemon verdict: UPGRADE NOW.**

**`clientAppVersion=0.8.0`: STAY.** This is sent in `hello` (`lib/paseo/transport.dart:231,315`) alongside only implemented capabilities (`:320`), not a daemon installation pin. Latest upstream [session code](https://github.com/getpaseo/paseo/blob/v0.9.2/packages/server/src/server/session.ts) still gates all-provider visibility at 0.1.45 and explicit workspace recovery at 0.1.105; 0.8.0 already exceeds both. Newer subscription/timeline features are capability-gated. Blindly copying 0.9.2 claims a newer upstream-client baseline without implementing it and buys no established benefit. Retain the number until a deliberate hello/capability contract migration; continue testing actual 0.9.2 daemon compatibility.

### Codex: verified app-server 0.153.4 → stable CLI 0.157.1

**What is actually pinned.** `lib/codex/transport.dart:1`, `lib/codex/gateway.dart:1`, `lib/codex/account.dart:6` and fixtures describe the verified 0.153.4 contract; there is no managed Codex installer/version enforcement in this slice. `clientInfo.version='1.0.0'` at `lib/codex/transport.dart:237` identifies this Flutter client and is not the CLI version. npm `@openai/codex` latest is 0.157.1; seven stable Rust releases follow the baseline (.154.0, .155.0, .155.1, .156.0, .156.1, .157.0, .157.1), with [1,116 compare commits](https://github.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.153.4...rust-v0.157.1). The 0.157.1 notes explicitly contain no determined highlights; do not invent its changes from the version number.

**Useful changes/security.** [0.154.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.154.0) improves remote resume/fork permission preservation, pre-trust helper execution safety, coordinated MCP OAuth refresh and approval context retention. [0.155.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.155.0) persists accepted prompts even if compaction fails and invalidates account-scoped caches/remote-control state after account changes. [0.156.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.156.0) preserves partial streamed answers on failure/interruption, closes Linux/macOS privileged-socket sandbox gaps, updates TLS dependencies (including musl OpenSSL 3.6.4) and improves proxy login. [0.157.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.157.0) adds current Sol/Luna catalog entries, retries transient uploads and enforces network restrictions across redirects and ongoing HTTP/WebSocket traffic. These warrant prompt host-side evaluation; no CVE number was asserted without an advisory. TUI voice/fullscreen/analytics changes do not add corresponding Flutter capabilities.

**Concrete protocol audit.** The app initializes with `experimentalApi:false` (`lib/codex/transport.dart:235-238`). Comparing both tags' generated JSON schemas for `ThreadStartParams`, `ThreadResumeParams`, `ThreadReadParams`, `ThreadListParams`, `ThreadDeleteParams`, `TurnStartParams`, `TurnInterruptParams`, `GetAccountResponse`, and `GetAccountRateLimitsResponse` found no removed top-level property or newly required top-level input. Additions include optional `originators` filtering, `disabledPluginIds`, and account rate-limit `ordinaryUsageAllowed`. This is a bounded schema check, not complete proof that all nested enums, policies and notification semantics are compatible. Exact call sites: `lib/codex/gateway.dart:238,275,317,338,367,455,489,540`; account `lib/codex/account.dart:83`. Source schemas: [0.153.4](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.153.4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/json/v2), [0.157.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/json/v2).

The gateway understands two approval request kinds and explicitly rejects unsupported requests (`lib/codex/gateway.dart:743-765`); new questions/user-verification/permission interactions do not become supported just because the server upgrades. Recheck resumed threads open in another client, account login/rate limits, command/file approvals and unknown-request rejection. Deprecated `codex mcp-server` was removed in .154.0; this app uses `codex app-server` (`docs/codex-connection.md:20`) and is not affected by that command removal. npm still ships Linux arm64, but this app's documented connection is to a user-owned remote host; Linux sandbox support cannot be assumed under Android/proot. **Verdict: UPGRADE LATER for the app's declared supported baseline**, after `test/codex_transport_test.dart`, `test/codex_gateway_test.dart`, `test/codex_account_session_test.dart`, `test/codex_journey_test.dart` and a protected real 0.157.1 WebSocket session pass. This is not advice to freeze security updates on independently maintained remote hosts; those can be evaluated separately, since no app installer pin prevents them.

**Existing-install delivery matters for all runtime verdicts.** A pin edit does not itself update a phone. OpenCode `setup()` explicitly calls `install_runtime "$requested_version"` (`lib/termux/bridge.dart:1667`), but generation switching probes the existing target first and installs only if absent (`:1899-1907`); ordinary restart likewise uses the existing version (`:1992-1996`). Validate the explicit setup/update path on an already-installed phone, as well as clean install, and assert the observed installed version. Paseo's install/repair action does rerun `npm_install "@getpaseo/cli@$paseo_version"` (`:3778`) even when Node is already present; merely starting the existing daemon does not do so. That action also updates unpinned Claude Code (`:3782`), so capture the resulting Claude version and recheck its root/proot wrapper and a real permitted turn instead of attributing all observed changes solely to Paseo.

### Node.js v24.21.0 → v26.10.0 Current — STAY on latest LTS

The verified pin and both checksums are `lib/termux/bridge.dart:3184–3189`. [Node's distribution index](https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json) reports **v24.21.0 still latest 24.x/LTS** (Krypton; 2026-09-07), while **v26.10.0** is latest non-prerelease Current (2026-09-21). There are **zero LTS releases behind**. The v26 train has 15 releases total, 3 published after the pin's date; that is not a linear patch backlog. [GitHub compare](https://github.com/nodejs/node/compare/v24.21.0...v26.10.0) is **diverged** (4,921 commits on target side, 3,734 on base side), not “4,921 missing fixes.” Read v26.0–v26.10 release notes, including security releases 26.3.1 and 26.5.1.

New [26.0](https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v26.0.0) APIs (Temporal, V8 14.6, Undici8) and later Web Workers, FFI/VFS, histogram/benchmark tools, crypto APIs and `openAsBlobSync` do not correspond to app-written Node logic. This app downloads Node (`bridge.dart:3670`), calls npm with IPv4 DNS ordering (`3719`), starts third-party agents, and probes `node-pty` through `module.createRequire` (`3792`). The node26 removals (`http.Server.writeHeader`, legacy `_stream_*`, `--experimental-transform-types`) have no direct use in these scripts; risk lies in installed CLI dependencies. Native module ABI changes **137→147**: qualify Paseo's node-pty/prebuild availability and reinstall/rebuild native modules, rather than replacing Node below an existing global prefix and assuming terminals work.

A concrete new runtime prerequisite exists: [Node26 BUILDING.md](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.10.0/BUILDING.md) says official Linux binaries require **libatomic from Node25 onward**. `install_node` only unpacks and executes the binary (`bridge.dart:3700–3709`); this flow does not explicitly install libatomic. GNU/Linux arm64 is Tier1 with kernel≥4.18/glibc≥2.28, but that is not an Android/proot guarantee. Ubuntu24 glibc satisfies the userspace floor; ABI/prebuilt addon/syscall validation is still needed on a phone. No measured RSS or thermal benefit justifies leaving LTS. Keep existing io_uring/DNS compatibility behavior when testing a future version.

Security is not a reason to jump majors here: [24.18.1](https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v24.18.1), already behind our pin, includes the July fixes also in 26.5.1, including CVE-2026-56848, -58043, -56850, -58040, -58041, -58042, -58045, -56847, -58039 and -58044 (and 24.x's -56846). Both current versions report OpenSSL3.5.8. This is release-note evidence, not a blanket claim that the runtime has no vulnerabilities. Reconsider 26 after LTS and explicit Paseo/Claude/native-terminal qualification, with checksums, libatomic and both arm64/x64 probes.

### Ubuntu Base: two actual pins, not one — refresh Termux within Noble

The requested `lib/termux/bridge.dart:1578` directory is `24.04`, but filenames pin **24.04.4** at 1582/1586/1590 and marker at 1611. The separate built-in engine already pins **24.04.5** (`android/app/src/main/kotlin/io/github/eslamasabry/opencode_mobile/BuiltinLinux.kt:809–818`). Canonical's [Noble Base directory and SHA256SUMS](https://cdimage.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-base/releases/24.04/release/) verify 24.04.5 as newest Noble image; [Resolute Base](https://cdimage.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-base/releases/26.04/release/) verifies **26.04.1** as latest overall, including arm64/armhf/amd64 images. “Behind” is one Noble image refresh for Termux and zero for built-in; OS image contents do not have a meaningful unified commit count.

The [24.04.5 announcement](https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-5-lts-released/87608/) describes integrated security/high-severity fixes and fewer initial downloads while retaining Noble compatibility. That is useful for slow proot/phone setup; it does not upgrade already-created userlands. No Base-specific changed-package manifest was exposed in the release directory, and the retrieved historical Noble point-change page did not establish a complete 24.04.4→.5 package/CVE delta. Therefore specific CVEs fixed in this rootfs archive remain **unverified**, rather than borrowed from desktop/kernel advisories.

The [24.04→26.04 LTS change summary](https://github.com/ubuntu/ubuntu-release-notes/blob/main/docs/26.04/summary-for-lts-users.md) changes glibc2.39→2.43, Python3.12→3.14, systemd255→259, coreutils to rust-coreutils, and apt's TLS/hash implementation to OpenSSL. Kernel, desktop and systemd boot improvements are largely irrelevant to this userland running atop Android, while glibc/syscalls and command behavior could affect almost every generated setup script. Concrete qualification surfaces are proot startup/environment (`BuiltinLinux.kt:172,231`), rootfs preparation/apt fake-root handling (`632–649`), all shell downloads/hash/extract/process logic in `bridge.dart`, and Python installation (`lib/builtin/setup/components.dart:187–195`). Fresh Base26 images exist, but no upstream release statement certifies this app's Android/proot environment. Stay with Noble until a dedicated fresh-rootfs and preserved-data migration rehearsal proves all local runtimes; never overwrite an existing rootfs as an “upgrade.”


## Per-component notes — Priority 3: direct pub dependencies

Live `https://pub.dev/api/packages/<name>` responses were read on 2026-09-27, including every version's publication date and latest pubspec; latest archive `CHANGELOG.md`, pubspec and native Gradle files were downloaded outside the worktree. Counts below mean **stable semantic versions newer than the lockfile resolution and no newer than latest**, excluding prereleases and lower-major backports published afterward. There is no release interval to summarize when resolved equals latest. `pubspec.yaml` caret lower bounds are not installed versions. No dependency resolution, app compilation or runtime test was performed in this research.

The mandated Flutter 3.47.1 cache actually carries **Dart 3.13.1** (cache version metadata), while `environment.sdk: ^3.10.0` means >=3.10.0 <4.0.0, not a Dart 3.10 compiler pin. Thus packages needing Dart 3.11/3.12 below fit the mandated SDK; they would not fit a hypothetical Dart 3.10 installation. Existing Android baseline is AGP **9.3.2**, Kotlin **2.4.0** (`android/settings.gradle.kts:22,25`), built-in Kotlin enabled and legacy DSL retained (`android/gradle.properties:5-6`), Java **17**, compileSdk **37** (`android/app/build.gradle.kts:22,26-27`); min/target/NDK inherit Flutter (`:23,32-33`). None of the examined latest direct pub packages declares a newer Flutter/Dart minimum than the real pinned SDK. Native Gradle source review is compatibility evidence, not proof of a successful native build or physical arm64 run.

Flutter plugins run in the Android app process, **outside Ubuntu/proot**; Linux support in a plugin does not imply it should be installed inside proot. Pure Dart packages have no arm64/proot ABI constraint. Native arm64 risks apply principally to sherpa's bundled libraries, recorder, camera and secure-storage platform implementations. No CVE identifier was stated in the reviewed newer pub-package release intervals; that is not a claim of a full vulnerability audit.

### mobile_scanner: 7.4.0 → 7.4.2 — UPGRADE NOW

Stable interval is 7.4.1 and 7.4.2; registry publication dates September 9 and 14 (7.4.2 changelog labels September 10). 7.4.1 guarantees CameraX `ImageProxy` release on failed/cancelled ML Kit work, fixing a permanently frozen decoder while preview continued. CameraX initialization failure reaches the normal error callback instead of crashing the host. It fixes start/switch/180-degree orientation handling, supplies ML Kit ProGuard retention, and removes the false-positive AGP 9 Kotlin warning by switching to Kotlin DSL with conditional KGP. 7.4.2 defers the orientation sensor listener until camera start, relevant to avoiding needless sensor work on a phone. Web/Apple fixes are not the Android motivation. [Changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/mobile_scanner/versions/7.4.2/changelog), [sensor fix](https://github.com/juliansteenbakker/mobile_scanner/commit/f9c81ea0b573d9146889fc70b599bf1f3920e35c).

App contact points: lazy `MobileScannerController` at `lib/ui/kit/kit_scanner.dart:499-500`, start/error conversion `:518-522`, stop/dispose `:530-543`, preview `:553`, lifecycle stops/restarts `:178-205`. These make lifecycle/rotation/resource bugs directly relevant. No removed Dart API in this interval. Latest native Gradle specifies compileSdk 36, minSdk 23, Java 17, CameraX 1.6.1; app's 37/Java17/AGP9.3.2 clears those declared requirements. Bundled ML Kit remains the default (17.3.0), preserving offline/no-Play-Services scanning. Native camera stays outside proot. Actual memory savings are not quantified by upstream.

### flutter_secure_storage: 11.0.0 → 11.2.0 — UPGRADE NOW

Count **11.1.0, 11.1.1, 11.2.0**; 10.3.2–10.3.4 published after 11.0.0 are maintenance-line backports, not versions ahead of 11.0.0. New `checkUpgradeStatus()` reports data loss from a direct major jump; Android fixes move wrapped keys across historical namespace options, use a saved key-cipher marker rather than `toString()`, port shared-key multi-instance fixes, scope `deleteAll` to prefix rather than clearing the whole preferences file, and repair biometric cancellation/recovery. Darwin keychain search now covers differing accessibility levels. These are security/data-integrity fixes, with no CVE named. [11.1.0–11.2.0 changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_secure_storage/versions/11.2.0/changelog), [shared-key fix](https://github.com/juliansteenbakker/flutter_secure_storage/commit/6cc9ddc55df42255edd4afb72bac56458997885d), [prefix deletion](https://github.com/juliansteenbakker/flutter_secure_storage/commit/34170b2caf52c642efa5b6584fa4cc5072f6c697).

`ProfileStore` creates default secure storage (`lib/state/profiles.dart:701-702`) and reads/writes/deletes credentials (`:734,740,792-802,924`); `OrchestrationStore` creates another default instance (`lib/state/orchestration_store.dart:85-86`); external agents share secure persistence (`lib/state/external_agents.dart:129,140,151,224`). Thus multi-instance correctness matters even though this app does not presently opt into biometrics, `storageNamespace`, or bulk `deleteAll`; do not claim those optional fixes are currently exercised. No app-call signature change between 11.0 and 11.2. Native latest remains minSdk24/Java17; it now uses `flutter.compileSdkVersion` instead of forcing 37, so this upgrade does not require raising the app's compileSdk. Keep the existing 37 pin pending full dependency/native validation. The old pre-v10-to-v11 credential-loss migration trap is **not undone** by 11.2; the new method detects loss, not recovers secrets.

It retains a compatibility AGP8.5.2/KGP1.8.22 buildscript workaround, so confirm real release build with our legacy-DSL flag before adoption. No phone performance or CVE fix established in this interval; arm64 Android SAF needs device read/import/save regression checks, not proot changes.

QrErrorCorrectLevel.M)`; replace with `QrCode(payload: QrPayload.fromString(data), errorCorrectLevel: QrErrorCorrectLevel.medium)` in a planned kit slice. ### Local generated SDK is not a pub package to replace

`packages/opencode_sdk/pubspec.yaml:1-8` is local version1.0.0, `publish_to:none`, generated from this repository's contracts. Its exact **dio5.11.0** at `:12` additionally constrains the app's `^5.7.0`: a Dio upgrade must first change generator source `tool/sdk/templates/pubspec.mustache:16` (and README template version), regenerate through `tool/sdk/generate.sh`, then validate generated-package analyzer/tests and app wire/SSE behavior. Never replace the local package with an unrelated pub name or hand-edit its generated output. flutter/flutter_localizations/flutter_test are similarly not independent hosted-package upgrades; their implementations move with the mandated Flutter cache.

### Dio 5.11.0 → 5.11.1 — UPGRADE NOW

Exact proposed future change: update the generator source `tool/sdk/templates/pubspec.mustache:16` from `dio: 5.11.0` to `dio: 5.11.1`, update the documented Dio version at `tool/sdk/templates/README.mustache:30`, and regenerate using `tool/sdk/generate.sh`. The generated SDK currently requires **exactly** 5.11.0 at `packages/opencode_sdk/pubspec.yaml:12`, so a root-only lockfile refresh cannot select 5.11.1 despite root `dio: ^5.7.0`. Regenerate (never hand-edit the generated package), deliberately update the SDK/root resolutions with the pinned toolchain, and verify deterministic regeneration. Do not refresh unrelated dependencies indiscriminately.

The September 4 patch fixes a paused response stream failing to pause its underlying socket subscription, which kept buffering into memory. That is directly relevant to persistent SSE traffic on memory-constrained phones: `lib/api/opencode_api.dart:253,270`, `lib/api2/transport.dart:270`, `lib/orchestration/client/http.dart:311`, and quota response streaming at `lib/quota/provider_quota_client.dart:44`. It also fixes `implements Interceptor` dispatch throwing `NoSuchMethodError`; our `PerfTraceInterceptor` **extends** Interceptor (`lib/diagnostics/perf_trace.dart:577`), so this second fix is not a present app trigger. A certificate-pinning change concerns the upstream test, not a newly announced app security fix. There is no declared public API break or native/AGP requirement change; Dart >=2.18<4 is compatible. Pure Dart networking runs in the Flutter process on Android/arm64; it is not installed inside proot. [Published changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/dio/versions/5.11.1/changelog), [release metadata](https://pub.dev/api/packages/dio).

Re-verify generated SDK `dart analyze` / `dart test`, including `tool/sdk/runtime/test/sse_transport_test.dart` and `http_wire_test.dart` in generated form, then `test/api2_transport_test.dart`, `test/api2_sse_test.dart`, `test/connection_sse_*_test.dart`, `test/server_probe_test.dart`, plus orchestration SSE reconnect/cancellation and quota streaming. Add or exercise an actual paused large-stream consumer against a local server and observe socket backpressure / bounded memory; ordinary small fixtures alone will not prove this fix. Verify auth headers and diagnostic redaction remain intact. Run final integration gates only when implementing a candidate; none were run for this research.

### dynamic_color 1.9.0 → 2.1.0 — STAY at 1.9

Four intervening stable releases: 2.0.0, 2.0.1, 2.0.2, 2.1.0 (all August 20). 2.0.0 moves to `material_ui` ^1.0.0 / material_color_utilities ^0.13.0; 2.0.1 fixes documentation; 2.0.2 conditionally applies Kotlin only below AGP 9; 2.1.0 adds XDG portal accent-color support on Linux. The Linux feature is useful eventually, but the Dart type break is concrete: latest `lib/src/corepalette_to_colorscheme.dart` imports `package:material_ui/material_ui.dart` and returns its ColorScheme; our `DynamicColorPlugin.getCorePalette()` result becomes `palette.toColorScheme(...)` in `lib/main.dart:1370–1374`, passed into Flutter-material-typed arguments at `lib/ui/theme_packs.dart:111–112`. Simply raising the constraint fails type compatibility there. Either a deliberate palette-to-Flutter conversion or a broader UI migration is needed, beyond a package bump. Existing 1.9 already includes surface-role fixes and AGP 9 support. Latest native script uses Java 17, minSdk 24, conditional Kotlin, and Flutter compileSdk; AGP 9.3.2/Kotlin 2.4.0/compileSdk 37 here meet those requirements. Native host theme APIs support Android arm64; Linux desktop portal support is not useful to a headless Ubuntu proot. [Changelog](https://pub.dev/packages/dynamic_color/versions/2.1.0/changelog), [published source archive](https://pub.dev/api/archives/dynamic_color-2.1.0.tar.gz), [Kotlin fix issue](https://github.com/material-foundation/flutter-packages/issues/695).

## Evidence scope and security interpretation

Research used `gh release list/view`, `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/compare/<base>...<target>`, temporary upstream git histories/tagged source, `npm view`, `https://pub.dev/api/packages/<name>` plus published archives, Node's distribution index and Canonical image/checksum indexes. Release/commit links above are the evidence for individual decisions; local `file:line` references refer to the source revision at the top. Latest upstream values are a dated snapshot.

As an additional scoped check, an [OSV querybatch](https://google.github.io/osv.dev/post-v1-querybatch/) for the 33 hosted direct Pub packages at their resolved lockfile versions returned no advisory records. The same query for npm `opencode-ai@1.18.29`, `@opencode/cli@2.0.10`, `@getpaseo/cli@0.9.1` and `@openai/codex@0.153.4` returned none. GitHub's published repository-security-advisory endpoints for Gas City, Beads and Dolt also returned empty lists. These narrow negative results do **not** override the Go/gRPC advisories found in upstream commits, enumerate transitive/native vulnerabilities, or establish that any component is vulnerability-free. Relevant identified security work and its applicability are documented per component.

Unresolved evidence is explicit: the complete Ubuntu Base .4→.5 package/CVE manifest was unavailable; no new-runtime phone benchmark or native build was run; no future-version pairing/store migration was executed. Those are acceptance work for the corresponding upgrade, not completed validation. This research changes no code, runtime pins, pubspec, lockfiles, credentials, live services or release state.

### Full upstream change inventory — supporting runtimes

This inventory is deliberately independent of app relevance. Recommended upgrades remain the separate, smaller set in the main review. Beads and Dolt have complete commit-subject/URL ledgers below, including merges, docs, tests, CI, dependency bumps and reversions. Node lists all 15 stable 26.x releases and an unfiltered ledger of every commit named in those release notes; this is not the entire divergent 24→26 Git history. Ubuntu covers release-level topics, not an invented manifest of packages actually installed in Ubuntu Base.

#### Beads: the entire 1.2.2 → 1.3.0 change surface

Sources: [tagged changelog](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/v1.3.0/CHANGELOG.md), [release notes](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0), [complete comparison](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/compare/v1.2.2...v1.3.0). Both the withheld `[1.2.1]` work and new `[1.3.0]` work are included: 1.2.2 did not contain the former. The changelog has 187 top-level entries in those two sections, with some repeated across the breaking-change summary and detailed sections. The 1,350-commit ledger below is the complete comparison, not a selection of interesting commits.

**HTTP/API additions:** a standalone HTTP service; capability/context discovery; project-identity response header; externally registered backend support; bearer-token-file authentication with rotation/revocation; non-loopback authentication requirement; Host allowlist; structured problem/error codes. Reading covers issue detail/list/ready/search/query/count/related/stats; dependency list/count/tree/blocking/cycles; workspace config, memories and events. Mutation covers create/batchCreate, claim/claimNext/release, close/batchClose/reopen/update/batchApply/delete/sweep, compare-and-set metadata and dependency editing. Detail revisions and expected-version guards support optimistic concurrency; revisions become strings. Listing sort and brief projections are added; dependency-detail projections can be shortened. Directory/root fields become optional when the server cannot truthfully provide them. Known omissions include TLS, identity-based authorization and mutation hooks over HTTP.

**Work coordination:** expiring claims, heartbeat renewal, reclaim and unclaim; replica identity protects leases granted elsewhere; reclaim filters constrain cleanup, with summaries explaining guarded skips. Conditional assignee/status writes and pool-aware claiming provide atomic handoffs. Actor canonicalization distinguishes exact `--` from other separators. Cross-type blocking dependencies become permissible. Claims are verified after server writes, race errors receive bounded retry, and no-op/failed ownership changes stop fabricating success/history. There is no newly registered dedicated unapprove command; reopening an issue is separate from reversing completed execution.

**Event/history plane:** opt-in durable mutation journal, follow/export/prune operations, retention floors and explicit truncation refusal; full post-mutation snapshots and actor attribution, including dependency removals during deletes. Journal data is clone-local. Existing audit events move out of versioned state, auxiliary rows are rekeyed, sidecar interaction logs become opt-in, and provenance is carried through reopen. Multi-ID reopen and label operations record per-issue history; batch commit messages exclude transient wisp IDs. Hooks reach both direct and proxied mutation paths; HTTP mutation behavior remains explicitly separate.

**Federation and remote coordination:** sync combines pull/conflict detection/blocked-state recomputation/push with bounded push-race retries and distinct failure codes; conflict inspection/resolution tools complement it. Git-origin-derived Dolt remote adoption now requires consent. Remote-ahead migration may fast-forward only under bounded conditions; shared-server mode no longer silently migrates. Replica-local state remains outside synchronization. Purging dropped Dolt databases is explicitly opt-in and destructive at server scope.

**Storage/backend/public Go contracts:** only Dolt-backed modes and conformant registered backends are supported at the tag; historical SQLite-support prose in the withheld section is stale. Proxied-server operation, mode-switch migrations, backend registration and conformance profiles are expanded. The exported interfaces gain role accessors for claiming, ready claiming, reading, dependency editing and other operations; reclaim gains a filter parameter, reopen a provenance field, and orphan-handling API scaffolding is removed. Role implementations and semantic contracts are unified across direct/proxied paths. Explicit server-port configuration takes precedence over environment hints. The CLI profiling option is renamed. Backend selection, store ownership and project identity are validated rather than guessed; legacy metadata gets targeted recovery guidance.

**Migration/maintenance:** schema53→66 plus clone-local0011→0026; migration freeze gates writes and implicit side effects; old binaries refuse newer schemas; shared stores require designated consent. Migration gate locks, force consent and server-mode schema migration are documented. Duplicate dependency rekeys, missing/incorrect clone-local cursors, tracked ignored-migration tables and encoding-drift failures receive repairs. Existing shared identity is adopted instead of overwritten. `doctor` obeys readonly/freeze policy. Cleanup/compaction perform full GC, export recovers after deletions, incremental export uses its intended path, explicit commits handle the whole working set and expose no-ops. Proxied opens stop rerunning migrations on every operation, and unnecessary schema-init serialization is removed. A known1.3.0 gap remains for absent event tables; the release notes point to a later1.3.1 fix.

**CLI behavior and compatibility:** done-status updates enforce close policy; search defaults include closed work; list-all includes pinned work while human-list defaults exclude finished/frozen/pinned items. Noninteractive empty-ID writes fail. Two competing text-input sources are rejected. Ready mode rejects unsupported filters and respects label-any/directory scope; proxied ready claims reject unimplementable row caps. Dependency-type validation matches the32-character storage bound. Cycle output gets a deterministic typed shape with partial members; multi-ID dependency output remains stable on errors. Multi-label mutation is per-item rather than whole-batch atomic. `--readonly serve` fails. Config reads no longer reveal the memory/KV plane. Hook chain/force flags become accepted no-ops. Redirected-stdin import is refused when unsupported. Terminal-only wording, creator labels, whitespace-label warnings/doctor checks and close-reason rendering improve operator output.

**Issue/dependency/wisp correctness:** delete-force orphans while explicit cascade removes dependents; missing IDs/referrers can refuse an entire delete; text-reference rewriting is transactional; cascade no longer marks unrelated live issues deleted. Purge/prune selection and deletion are atomic and tier-aware; dry-run/pattern behavior agrees with actual execution. Batch creation is atomic and honors plan-level flags, occupied explicit IDs fail, and parent/child counters stay consistent. Ephemeral/no-history transitions move both issue and dependency data correctly. Reopening custom done statuses works. Parent reassignment no longer leaves a stale parent. Wisp-edge removal, cross-repository dependency errors, vanished claim rows and stale labels are corrected. Query OR/NOT logic, malformed row-cap errors, ready totals, partial-ID dependency trees, canonical blocker ordering, count/filter parity, custom types/status refresh and typed metadata/subsecond time roundtrips are repaired. Labels are normalized consistently; shell wildcards in show output survive rendering.

**Performance/resource changes:** narrower issue/dependency payloads, fewer telemetry subprocesses and machine-ID probes, queued-only throttled metric flush, no stranded telemetry backlog after opting out, conditional server backup, functioning deferred auto-commit policy, fewer schema locks/migrations, incremental exports and idle-reaping proxied backends. Active proxy memory can exceed direct-server memory, so idle savings are not universal. FreeBSD compilation is repaired; native Android assets also exist. No claimed Android phantom-process-killer removal accompanies these changes.

**Security/docs/tooling:** Go1.26.7 build and dependency-security updates, reachability-scoped advisory accounting, token-safe authentication errors, remote-adoption consent and memory-plane disclosure fixes. Wisp-plane migration corpora, backend contract/conformance matrices, CI flakes and migration error propagation are improved. Documentation explicitly records unsupported multi-rig prefix routing, lease/heartbeat/re-home invariants, upgrade/rollback procedures and operational caveats. The commit ledger retains every additional test/doc/CI/refactor/dependency entry without relevance filtering.

#### Dolt: both patch releases, without relevance filtering

[2.3.4](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/tag/v2.3.4) includes journal bootstrap cancellation repair; warning for noninteractive session-only checkout; cached tag/branch name indexes; persistent SQL mode reload; vector-index nullability validation at DDL rather than schema load; generated-column exclusion in SQL diffs; shell cancellation; foreign-key dropped-column correctness; test-driver gRPC1.83.2; and distinct treatment of empty versus comment-only shell statements.

Its SQL-engine changes cover vector DDL tests; aggregate statistical return types; numeric-to-date conversion; refusal of unsupported DISTINCT windows; nested subquery alias analysis; CHAR trailing-space equality; window partition/order identity; pluggable update-assignment evaluation; grouped-window/iterator-cleanup tests; prepared binding and user-variable representation; subquery/scalar alias rendering; general expression descriptions; replacement-tree notification for aliased projections; multibyte padding and collation derivation; coercibility/binary-collation detection; BIGINT overflow; empty inserts with generated columns; descending indexes/NULL ordering; aliases inside window clauses; and EXISTS over ungrouped aggregates. Closed-issue lists additionally track window/range/NTILE errors, auto-GC ignored-table loss and canceled git-remote transport hangs; an issue appearing closed is not proof that its fix first entered this exact patch range.

[2.3.5](https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/releases/tag/v2.3.5) includes wildcard binlog replication filters and lifecycle synchronization; structural merging for adaptive-JSON encoding; legacy table-name unmarshalling repair; LOAD_FILE directory-handle cleanup; partial-join/window EXISTS simplification; replication string-list values; date/time-to-number conversion; corrected inner-join decorrelation for EXISTS; automated dependency-bump validation/approval/merge; replication-filter parser syntax; and NULL ordering. Regression coverage also touches long-option prefixes, primary-key-change diffs, overlapping-index merges, prepared numeric values, large JSON integers, virtual columns, ignored-table behavior, resets, AS-OF parameters, aggregate grouping and statement boundaries. Again, historical issue closure and newly shipped implementation are distinguished by the complete105-commit ledger.

Unfiltered non-product work includes Unix Bats caching/tmpfs/matrix optimization, expect timeouts, server test harness adoption, MinIO download correction, build-tag support for consumers, generated formatting/dependency updates, SQL correctness metadata and release-version commits. The linked release performance tables are against MySQL, not before/after measurements against2.3.3.
